proposals.observation: Three CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: Weekly Queue Topup (17:55 UTC), Funnel-Hack Digest (09:03 UTC), and Daily Blog Post (03:58 UTC). The content queue sits at 1 post queued against 47 published. If the Daily Blog Post workflow stays broken, that single queued post is the last piece of scheduled content before the pipeline goes dark. The queue topup failure compounds this because the refill mechanism is also down.
proposals.proposal: Inspect and fix the Daily Blog Post workflow. The failure at 03:58 UTC is the most urgent because it is the direct publishing step. Check the workflow run logs for the specific error (likely an API key expiry, a changed content schema field, or a path that no longer resolves). Once the root cause is visible, patch only the broken step. Do not touch astro.config.mjs or src/content.config.ts, which are blocked paths. Ship the fix as a single edit to the workflow YAML.

proposals.impact: prevents queue running dry within days
proposals.observation: The Weekly Queue Topup workflow also failed (17:55 UTC). With the queue at 1 post, Joel has roughly one day of buffer before no content publishes at all. The topup workflow is the mechanism that generates new draft posts to keep the queue above a safe threshold. A second consecutive failure tomorrow would leave the content side of the funnel empty during a period when the email automations are actively running and sending warm subscribers to the site.
proposals.proposal: Inspect and fix the Weekly Queue Topup workflow independently of the Daily Blog Post fix. Treat these as two separate investigations because they failed at different times and likely have different root causes. The topup workflow almost certainly calls a generative step (LLM or template fill) followed by a git commit back to the repo. Common failure points are rate limits, a changed prompt template path, or a git push permission error after a token rotation. Fix the single failing step and verify the queue count rises above 5 before closing the issue.

proposals.impact: converts highest-open-rate sequence into booked calls
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends, the highest of the three active sequences. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. High open rates mean the subject line and sender trust are working, but open rate alone does not convert. There is no data showing click-throughs or replies from any automation, which suggests the email body is not giving Money Vigilance subscribers a clear reason to take the next step toward a coaching conversation.
proposals.proposal: Add a single grounded, specific call-to-action paragraph to the first email in the Money Vigilance automation. Money Vigilance subscribers are typically the most financially careful people in Joel's audience: they track, they restrict, they worry. The current email almost certainly explains their pattern back to them. That explanation needs one more sentence that opens a door toward a real conversation, written in the register Joel actually uses, not a generic "book a call" bolt-on.
